summary.text: An 80-year-old man with a history of atrial fibrillation, taking edoxaban 60 mg and prasugrel 3.75 mg, was brought to the emergency department with sudden-onset left hemiparesis and dysarthria. On arrival his GCS was E3V4M6 and NIHSS 12, with a prestroke mRS of 0. MRI showed an acute right MCA infarct and MRA a proximal M1 occlusion.

Intravenous alteplase was considered inappropriate because the INR was 4.52, and mechanical thrombectomy with a combined technique achieved complete reperfusion, TICI grade 3. A residual focal right MCA stenosis and retrograde collaterals led to a diagnosis of ICAD. Admission labs showed platelets of 51 and overt DIC was excluded. Whole-body CT after MT showed splenomegaly, pancytopenia progressed by day 4, and bone marrow examination on day 5 diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive ALL.

Prednisolone 60 mg was started on day 8 as part of induction therapy. On day 9 worsening anemia due to hematuria led to temporary discontinuation of DAPT, with edoxaban alone continued. On day 13 left hemiparesis and dysarthria recurred with reocclusion of the right M1 segment. DAPT was resumed and a second thrombectomy achieved TICI grade 3 reperfusion; intracranial PTA was then performed with a balloon catheter for residual stenosis.

Repeat angiography after PTA showed sustained vessel patency without residual stenosis or early recoil, with no flow-limiting dissection, distal embolization or perioperative complications. Left upper-limb weakness persisted but his neurological condition gradually improved. On day 21 he was transferred to another facility for further induction therapy for ALL with an mRS score of 4.
